messages:
mike: heads-up — noticed the embed splitter affinity case is putting entire large requests onto a single shard and we got a bunch of 413s + huge tail latency last night.

devin: can you paste a small repro or example payload? how big were the arrays / bytes?

mike: redacted example below:
```json
{"input": ["<base64-blob-1>", "<base64-blob-2>", "..."], "model": "embed-4-large", "options": {"split_policy": "affinity"}}
```
single request ~45MB total, ~800 vectors at 1024 dims.

priya: that makes sense. our affinity rule groups by request id to preserve ordering/dim-compat, but we never enforced a bytes-per-shard cap — so one shard gets the whole 45MB and trips OOM/413.

devin: confirmed. current splitter path is `split_by_dims_then_affinity()` and we assumed dims-splitting would bound sizes. edge-case: mixed-dim items + a few huge items => affinity defeats the bytes cap.

sara: telemetry gap here — Console shows aggregated `embeddings.413` but not why (split rejection vs model reject). we should emit `embeddings.splitter.reject_by_shard` and a `splitter.bytes_per_shard` histogram and tag traces with `split_strategy` so rollouts are observable.

mike: proposal:
- short-term: enforce per-shard byte cap (16MB) and return clearer error `413 PayloadTooLarge: split_per_shard_bytes_exceeded` with guidance
- medium: introduce client hint header `x-embed-preferred-split: interleave|affinity` so SDKs can opt into interleaving for large payloads
- observability: add metric tags `split_strategy=<affinity|interleave|auto>` and `split_reason=<dims|bytes|quota>` on counters and traces
- rollout plan: canary new splitter for 10% traffic, 3-day burn-in, monitor per-shard latency p99, 413 rate, and cost/tokens delta

priya: UX note for Console — show "suggested split" in request inspector with estimated shards and approximate unit-cost impact. that will help callers decide whether to chunk client-side.

devin: I'll open a PR to add the bytes-per-shard cap + metric tags. prefer not to change default heuristics yet; just fail-fast and gather metrics.

sara: +1. also add a short migration note in SDKs explaining `x-embed-preferred-split` and recommended safety limits.

ops-bot: deploy queued: pr/embeds-splitter-bytecap (#4321) :gear:

mike: thanks — assigning follow-ups to @devin and @priya. leaving this thread for async updates; will check metrics after canary starts.
